topline.text: A quieter 24-48 hours nationally, but Ofqual's third annual cyber security survey, published today, shows school cyber-attacks continuing to fall: 27% of secondaries hit by an incident in 2025/26, down from 34% two years ago, with recovery times also improving.
Closer to home: Barnsley Council's cabinet meets on 7 October to approve a £4.4m increase (to £7.37m total) for the 40-place specialist primary school planned at The Mill, Worsbrough Bridge.
topline.action: Worth flagging to SEND colleagues working with Barnsley families awaiting the new places.

diary.text: Barnsley Council cabinet considers the revised £7.37m budget for the Worsbrough Bridge specialist primary school.
Midday deadline for Sheffield secondary school applications for September 2027 entry.
NEU national executive reconvenes to decide whether to relaunch the paused strike ballot.

items.lede: Ofqual's latest poll shows fewer, less damaging cyber incidents.
items.body: The exam regulator's third annual Teacher Tapp survey, published today, found 27% of secondary schools and colleges were hit by a cyber incident in 2025/26, down from 29% the year before and 34% in 2023/24. Two-thirds of affected schools recovered immediately (up from 55%), and incidents causing critical damage fell to 7%. Ofqual still flags a responsibility gap: only 9% of staff say senior leadership owns cyber security, versus 46% pointing to IT teams.
items.action: Worth a line in the next SLT update confirming who in your school actually owns the cyber-incident response plan.

sections.heading: Sheffield/South Yorkshire: Barnsley's SEND place cost overrun

items.lede: Cost of 40 new SEND places in Barnsley rises by £4.4m.
items.body: Barnsley Council's cabinet meets on 7 October to approve a revised £7.37m budget - up from the plans approved last October - to refurbish The Mill at Worsbrough Bridge into a 40-place specialist primary school. Survey and design work found more extensive access and equipment needs than expected; the scheme remains fully funded by a ring-fenced government capital grant, with Waterton Academy Trust as preferred delivery partner.
items.action: A reminder that SEND capital schemes regularly cost more than first budgeted - useful context if you're advising on local place-planning timelines.

box.label: Jargon-buster - Ring-fenced grant
box.intro: Comes up in the Barnsley SEND funding story above.
box.text: Government money that can legally only be spent on the purpose it was awarded for (e.g. new SEND places) - a council can't redirect it to plug other budget gaps, but equally can't flex it if costs rise, as Barnsley's are now doing.
